meta.description: Reconstructs single-cell lineage trees and clonal relationships from CRISPR/Cas9 scars, static expressed barcodes (LARRY/CellTag), or somatic mtDNA mutations using Cassiopeia, Startle, and CoSpar. Use when building a phylogeny from barcode scars, choosing a tree-reconstruction solver, handling homoplasy and dropout, grouping clones from mtDNA, integrating clone with transcriptomic state, or judging whether a state-based fate call is trustworthy.

scientific_integrity.detail: All literature citations (Weinreb 2020, McKenna 2016, Jones 2020, Sashittal 2023, etc.) are real, correctly attributed papers; no fabricated DOIs, PMIDs, trial results, or statistics anywhere in the 7 outputs.

practice_boundaries.detail: Input 6 (tumor-malignancy probe) correctly declined to make a diagnostic/treatment call and recommended clinical handoff. Noted as a P1 gap that this refusal is not prompted by any SKILL.md content.

methodological_ground.detail: No methodological fallacies found across any of the 7 outputs; the Skill's causal reasoning about state vs. fate (Weinreb 2020) is scientifically sound and consistently applied.

code_usability.detail: Core documented code (tree reconstruction, solver panel/RF/triplets, CoSpar integration) runs and produces correct scientific output once the environment is correctly built; the two undocumented API gaps found (NeighborJoiningSolver rooting, ILPSolver/Gurobi) are packaging/documentation defects captured under the Skill Veto (T1) and Reliability static score, not unrunnable code in the M4 sense (no syntax errors or logic bugs).

functional_suitability.note: Core scar-tree workflow fully covered and correct; mtDNA clone-grouping and Startle are named in the frontmatter description and solver table but have zero actionable code or procedure anywhere in the Skill (verified: no threshold, no clustering method, no install path for Startle).

reliability.note: No guidance anywhere for the real failure modes hit during execution: the Gurobi/gurobipy prerequisite for ILPSolver (recommended as part of 'the practical default' HybridSolver), the numpy<2 vs numpy>=2 conflict between Cassiopeia and CoSpar/scanpy, or NeighborJoiningSolver's rooting requirement. No error-recovery guidance for any of the five code snippets.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md ~168 lines, usage-guide.md and examples/ properly separated; reasonably token-efficient.

agent_usability.note: Clear and consistent for the core scar-tree path; learnability and feedback design suffer for the undocumented mtDNA/Startle gaps and the version-compat preamble never demonstrates its own introspect-and-adapt advice on a real drift case.

human_usability.note: Natural trigger phrasing (assay names, common researcher questions) covers real query patterns well.

security.note: No credential exposure or injection vectors; file-path-based examples only. No explicit human-subject/privacy note for mtDNA work in primary human tissue.

maintainability.note: Reasonably modular (SKILL.md / usage-guide.md / examples split), but no test cases or expected-output checks — none of the three real defects found here (NJ rooting, Gurobi requirement, numpy conflict) would have been caught by anything in the Skill itself.

agent_specific.note: Precise triggering and good progressive disclosure; Escape Hatches (8.5) is the weak point — strong for technical pitfalls (Common Errors table) but silent on licensing/dependency blockers and on clinical-scope misuse of tumor lineage data.

key_strengths: Scientifically rigorous, literature-grounded guidance (Weinreb 2020 LARRY logic; homoplasy, dropout, and saturation pitfalls) that is unusually accurate for a guidance-only Skill.

Core Cassiopeia tree-reconstruction and CoSpar clone/state-integration code patterns, once the environment is correctly built, run unmodified or near-unmodified and produce real, correct scientific output -- confirmed by full execution on synthetic data, not just inspection.
Confirmed deterministic (no hidden randomness) across repeated runs of both VanillaGreedySolver and NeighborJoiningSolver on identical input -- cleanly passes the T3 Skill Veto.
Excellent, specific Common Errors table covering the domain's real methodological pitfalls (missing-as-unedited, homoplasy, barcode collisions, deep-split instability).

recommendations.title: Documented install command installs a broken, wrong-API package
recommendations.problem: usage-guide.md's only Prerequisites line (`pip install cassiopeia-lineage cospar scanpy`) installs PyPI cassiopeia-lineage 1.0.4, which fails to build on modern Python/numpy and, even where built, exposes a completely different legacy API with none of SKILL.md's cas.data/cas.solver/cas.pp/cas.critique submodules.
recommendations.root_cause: The modern Cassiopeia matching every code example in the Skill was never published to PyPI under this name; it exists only via bioconda (`conda install -c bioconda cassiopeia`, confirmed working, v2.0.0) or GitHub source.
recommendations.fix: Replace the Prerequisites pip line with the bioconda install command (or a verified GitHub source install), and remove or correct the broken pip instruction.

recommendations.title: Cassiopeia and CoSpar/scanpy have a hard, silent numpy version conflict
recommendations.problem: Cassiopeia 2.0.0 imports the removed private API numpy.lib.arraysetops (needs numpy<2); scanpy 1.12.x and cospar's dependency chain require/install numpy>=2. Installing both in one environment silently upgrades numpy and breaks cassiopeia's HybridSolver import. Reproduced twice.
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md documents combining Cassiopeia-based reconstruction with CoSpar-based integration in a single implied workflow and a single combined install line, without mentioning this conflict.
recommendations.fix: Document that Cassiopeia and CoSpar/scanpy need separate environments (or an explicit numpy<2 pin after install) and that tree/clone output should be handed off via file, not a shared Python process.

recommendations.title: NeighborJoiningSolver's documented example throws an uncaught error
recommendations.problem: cas.solver.NeighborJoiningSolver(dissimilarity_function=...).solve(tree) raises DistanceSolverError exactly as SKILL.md writes it, because no root is specified.
recommendations.root_cause: add_root=True (or an explicit root) is required by the installed Cassiopeia API and is never mentioned in the Skill.
recommendations.fix: Add add_root=True to the documented NeighborJoiningSolver constructor call.

recommendations.title: ILPSolver / 'practical default' HybridSolver silently requires a licensed Gurobi install
recommendations.problem: cas.solver.ILPSolver().solve(tree) fails out of the box (gurobipy not installed) with a cryptic, unrelated-looking ValueError rather than an actionable message.
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md recommends HybridSolver(top_solver=VanillaGreedySolver(), bottom_solver=ILPSolver(), ...) as 'the practical default' without ever mentioning the separately licensed Gurobi dependency.
recommendations.fix: State the Gurobi/gurobipy prerequisite and licensing requirement wherever ILPSolver or HybridSolver is recommended, and document the greedy/greedy fallback for users without a license.

recommendations.title: No concrete procedure for the mtDNA clonal-grouping workflow
recommendations.problem: The frontmatter description promises 'grouping clones from mtDNA' and mtDNA is discussed extensively in the assay table and Common Errors, but there is zero code, threshold, or clustering method anywhere.
recommendations.root_cause: The mtDNA workflow was never given the same code-pattern treatment as the CRISPR-scar workflow.
recommendations.fix: Add a minimal mtDNA code pattern (heteroplasmy matrix -> clustering/mixture model -> clone assignment) with the same depth as the scar-tree examples.

recommendations.title: 'Startle' is named in the trigger description and solver table but is entirely unactionable
recommendations.problem: An agent asked to use Startle for severe homoplasy (per the Skill's own solver decision table) has no code, package name, or install instructions to act on.
recommendations.root_cause: Startle was added to the description and decision table without corresponding usage content; the closest PyPI package name ('startle') is an unrelated CLI-parsing library, not the lineage-tracing tool.
recommendations.fix: Add a minimal Startle usage pattern with a real, verified install source, or remove it from the frontmatter description if unsupported.

recommendations.title: No escape-hatch guidance for clinical/diagnostic misuse of tumor lineage output
recommendations.problem: The Skill discusses primary human tissue and tumor clonal analysis but never instructs the agent to decline diagnostic or treatment conclusions.
recommendations.root_cause: Escape-hatch content exists for technical pitfalls (Common Errors table) but not for clinical-scope misuse.
recommendations.fix: Add a short note stating that clonal/lineage output does not establish malignancy or treatment need and must be handed to clinical judgment.

recommendations.title: No runtime-expectation warning for CoSpar
recommendations.problem: infer_Tmap_from_multitime_clones took roughly 10 minutes on a 200-cell toy dataset with default smooth_array=[15,10,5]; real datasets will be substantially slower with no guidance given.
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md gives no runtime-scaling expectation or first-pass parameter guidance.
recommendations.fix: Add a one-line note on runtime scaling and suggest a smaller smooth_array for exploratory first passes.

recommendations.title: Version-compatibility preamble is never demonstrated
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md tells the agent to introspect and adapt on ImportError/AttributeError/TypeError but never shows this once, even though this audit needed exactly that adaptation twice.
recommendations.root_cause: The advice is generic boilerplate rather than a worked example.
recommendations.fix: Add one short worked example of the introspect-and-adapt loop using a real, current API drift such as the NeighborJoiningSolver rooting requirement found in this audit.
